delta_text: The user is asking about the trade-offs between eager and lazy loading in a module-based architecture. I should explain that eager loading resolves every dependency at startup, which makes failures surface early and keeps the dependency graph easy to reason about, while lazy loading defers resolution until a module is first used, which improves cold-start latency for large trees.
The core trade-off is predictability versus startup cost: eager loading pays for modules that may never be touched, but lazy loading can fail mid-session if a deferred dependency is missing.

For a CLI agent harness where every invocation is a fresh process, cold-start matters, so lazy loading is generally the better default, with explicit eager loading reserved for modules on the hot path.
Eager loading resolves all dependencies at startup; lazy loading defers resolution until first use. For a CLI harness, prefer lazy loading with explicit eager loading for hot-path modules.
